audit.recode_to: 'descriptions disagree' between Oliveira 1993:55-58 (count-based general rule: 2-3σ penult, 4+σ antepenult, with morpheme-specific overrides) and Aikhenvald 1995:9-10 (contrastive stress; placement 'depends on the accentual properties of morphemes'; prefixes extraprosodic, suffixes accented vs extraprosodic; polysyllables only bounded by an antepenult window; final nasal vowels always stressed) — or, if one class must be chosen, the catalog's lexical/morphological-accent class with a right-edge three-syllable window and penult default (StressTyp2-style P;LEX) rather than pure count-dependent 'fixed'. Either way: add Aikhenvald 1995:9 as co-source, delete the 'different last speaker' conjecture (same consultant, Candelário da Silva, 1991), and note that StressTyp2's paraphrase 'longer words have penultimate stress with antepenultimate exceptions' over-reads p.9 (that sentence is about trisyllables; for polysyllables Aikhenvald states only the antepenult window).
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold

It is a legitimate primary and the most detailed stress treatment that exists, but it was the only primary read; the published grammar by the thesis supervisor (Aikhenvald 1995, the StressTyp2/WALS source) was unreached and only StressTyp2's paraphrase was carried. (3) I located an open copy of Aikhenvald 1995 uploaded by the author herself to the Internet Archive, saved it under, and read p.9-10 as page images. sources.quote: p.9: 'Bare has contrastive stress, e.g. the following minimal pair: kuɻí "surubim: a kind of fish" and kúɻi "a spring". In disyllabic monomorphemic words, the stress falls most frequently on the first syllable, e.g. mába "bee", dápa "pacca". Occasionally, the last syllable is stressed, e.g. beké "future marker". In trisyllabic words the stress falls most frequently on the penultimate syllable, e.g. mukáwa "rifle", yawáke "yesterday", more rarely it falls on the antepenultimate syllable, e.g. i-d'ékada "he made". sources.locator: §1.3.1.1 'Stress', p.9 (PDF p.7, right half of spread); §1.3.1.2 p.10; abstract (PDF p.1)
sources.note: The published grammar and the StressTyp2 (P;LEX) / WALS 14A source; our record codes count-based fixed stress from the supervisee's MA thesis alone and carried only StressTyp2's paraphrase of p.9. now obtained: p.9 frames Baré stress as contrastive and morpheme-driven inside a final three-syllable window, without Oliveira's '4+ syllables -> antepenult' clause.
